Description

Staff Accountant

About the role

We are hiring Staff Accountants to work 100% remotely from Mexico for small and mid-sized companies and CPA firms in the US.

What you will do

  • Run the monthly close: journal entries, accruals, prepaids, depreciation and payroll entries.
  • Reconcile bank, credit card, AP, AR and balance sheet accounts every month.
  • Prepare monthly financial statements and variance explanations for the controller or owner.
  • Maintain fixed asset, loan and lease schedules.
  • Support year-end: prepare audit or tax packages for the outside CPA.
  • Review the bookkeeper's or AP/AR specialist's work and fix coding errors.
  • Improve close checklists and spreadsheets so each month gets faster.

What you bring

Must have

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting (Contaduría Pública) or finance.
  • 3+ years in general accounting with ownership of month-end close.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. GAAP concepts: accrual accounting, revenue recognition, balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Intermediate-to-advanced English (B2+) for written reports and calls with the controller.
  • Advanced Excel: pivot tables, lookups, building reconciliation schedules.

Nice to have

  • Experience at a U.S. company, a Big 4 or mid-tier firm, or an outsourced accounting firm serving U.S. clients.
  • QuickBooks Online, NetSuite, Sage Intacct or Xero.
  • Job costing or WIP schedules for construction or manufacturing.

Requirements

Staff Accountant

Must Have:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • 3+ years of general accounting experience.
  • Hands-on ownership of month-end close.
  • Knowledge of U.S. GAAP, accruals, journal entries, and balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Experience preparing financial statements and variance analysis.
  • Advanced Excel (pivot tables, lookups, reconciliation schedules).
  • English B2+ for professional communication and financial reporting.
  • Experience with U.S. companies, CPA firms, or outsourced accounting firms.
  • QuickBooks Online, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, or Xero.
  • Experience with fixed assets, loans, leases, and audit/tax support.
  • Job costing or WIP schedules in construction or manufacturing.

description:
Clinigen is a rapidly growing global specialty pharmaceutical services business with a unique combination of services across the pharmaceutical lifecycle. We currently have over 1,000 employees headquartered in the UK with global offices in the US, EU (Belgium, Germany, France), Asia Pacific and South Africa.

Are you looking to shape the tax strategy behind global pharmaceutical services?

If so, we are seeking an indirect tax specialist who enjoys solving complex commercial challenges, influencing business decisions and working across international markets.

The Role:

Clinigen is looking for a Head of Indirect Tax to play a key role in supporting its global pharmaceutical services business. Reporting to the Group Head of Tax, this is an opportunity to combine technical VAT expertise with commercial advisory work, partnering with senior stakeholders to support business growth, optimise supply chains and manage tax risk across multiple jurisdictions.

The Opportunity

This is a highly commercial, advisory-led position, with approximately 80% of the role focused on advisory work and 20% on compliance. You'll work closely with Commercial, Business Development, Finance, Legal and Supply Chain teams, providing VAT and indirect tax guidance on new business opportunities, complex cross-border transactions, commercial agreements and strategic projects, including specialist areas such as Managed Access and cell and gene therapies.

Alongside your advisory responsibilities, you'll oversee VAT compliance across the UK, Europe and Australia, manage relationships with HMRC and external tax advisers, lead on audits, and ensure robust tax controls, reporting processes and systems. You'll also lead and develop the indirect tax team, helping shape how the function evolves as technology and AI transform tax processes.

What We're Looking For

We're keen to hear from candidates with strong technical VAT and indirect tax expertise, experience advising on complex commercial arrangements and international supply chains, and the confidence to influence stakeholders at all levels. Experience gained within a Big Four or comparable tax advisory environment would be particularly valuable, alongside a commercially minded approach and the ability to translate technical tax matters into practical business solutions.

Pharmaceutical or life sciences experience with a recognised tax or accounting qualification is expected.

Why Clinigen?

This is an opportunity to step beyond traditional VAT compliance and take on a visible, commercially influential role within a specialist global pharmaceutical services business. You'll have broad international exposure, work on technically challenging projects and help shape the future of the indirect tax function, with flexible remote working arrangements available.

*Annual salary review

Interested in making a broader commercial impact with your indirect tax expertise? We'd love to hear from you.

excerpt: At Forrester, we’re trusted to work on trailblazing, mission critical problems that business and technology leaders face today.
description:
At Forrester, we’re trusted to work on trailblazing, mission critical problems that business and technology leaders face today. That’s why we’re always looking to empower talented individuals to perform at their best every single day. We’re proud of our community of smart people and vibrant voices who come together to do what’s right by our clients and each other. Our success is driven by curiosity, courage and customer obsession. The confidence and drive to be bold at work. Join us and build an extraordinary future.

About This Role:

Forrester Research is seeking a Principal Analyst to lead research and advisory coverage of IT service management (ITSM), enterprise service management (ESM), IT operations management (ITOM) and the evolution of modern IT operations. This individual will help technology leaders modernize how they design, deliver, support, measure, and continuously improve technology services across the enterprise. The role requires a strong mix of strategic perspective, hands-on operational experience, market knowledge, and the ability to translate complex practices and technologies into clear, actionable advice for senior technology leaders.

The Principal Analyst will define a forward-looking research agenda spanning service management strategy, operating models, service desk modernization, incident and problem management, change enablement, service portfolio and catalog management, service-level management, experience and value measurement, and intelligent automation. The analyst may also contribute to adjacent AIOps coverage, particularly where observability, event intelligence, automation, and service management converge.

Job Description:

The Principal Analyst works as part of a high-performing team with a strong emphasis on collaborating with others in all aspects of the job. A Principal Analyst is expected to:

  • Lead Forrester’s service management and IT ops research, developing a differentiated portfolio that helps technology executives and operations leaders improve service quality, employee experience, operational efficiency, resilience, and business value. Contribute to research at the intersection of ITSM/ESM, IT operations management, observability, automation, and AIOps
  • Define the future of service management as AI, automation, agentic systems, observability, and platform strategies reshape service delivery, support, and operations. Examine the expansion of service management beyond IT into enterprise workflows and shared services, including the governance, ownership, process, data, and adoption requirements for successful ESM programs.
  • Conduct primary research through client interviews, surveys, vendor briefings, practitioner discussions, and market analysis. Turn that evidence into provocative, fact-based points of view and practical client guidance.
  • Advise clients on ITSM/ESM strategy and maturity, ITIL adoption, operating models, governance, practice ownership, organizational design, and the sequencing of modernization efforts.
  • Guide clients on core service management practices, including incident and major incident management, problem management, change enablement, request management, service desk operations, service portfolio and catalog management, service-level management, configuration management, and continual improvement.
  • Create high quality, actionable, analytically deep and fact-based research content throughout the year; i.e., write ~12 thought leading reports on an agreed upon research agenda per year + additional IP (tools, webinars, videos, etc.) to support our clients.
  • Build visibility for his/her research and contribute to Forrester client communities and beyond.
  • Drive and lead key Forrester Waves and Landscape research in the ITSM/ESM platform market, including major vendors, emerging providers, ecosystem partners, implementation considerations, platform selection, consolidation, replacement, and value realization.
  • Consult with clients to apply Forrester’s research in the context of their specific business environment and help solve their problems through inquiry, guidance, and advisory and consulting engagements.
  • Present at Forrester-sponsored and industry-related events and deliver client webinars.
  • Establish an industry presence as an influential speaker and thinker; build relationships with journalists who cover the sector; participate in vendor briefings and field press inquiries as necessary.
  • Support business development and prospect conversations as arranged by Forrester’s account leadership teams.
  • Fosters a leadership style that drives a culture of cross-team collaboration, mentorship, integrity and relentless and positive pursuits.

Job Requirements:

  • At least 10 years of experience in a mix of roles as a director-level and above practitioner, consultant, or research analyst in technology.
  • Demonstrated ability to serve as an advisor to senior management and C-level clients.
  • Superior client-facing communication, listening, critical thinking, and collaboration skills with researchers, subject-matter experts, and client leaders.
  • Deep knowledge of ITSM and ITIL principles, with practical experience designing, improving, governing, or operating service management capabilities at enterprise scale.
  • Strong expertise in several core practices such as incident and major incident management, problem management, change enablement, request management, service desk, service catalog and portfolio management, service-level management, configuration management, or continual improvement.
  • Experience with major ITSM/ESM platforms and a strong understanding of market dynamics, vendor differentiation, implementation approaches, and common adoption challenges.
  • Understanding of how AI, automation, virtual agents, observability, and data are changing service management and IT operations.
  • Ability to take complex, disparate ideas and distill them into simple, provocative concepts; willingness to take a stand on outcomes with clients, vendors, press, and competition.
  • Superior analytical, writing, editing, and presentation skills.
  • The ability to travel 30% of the time or more.

excerpt: COMPANY OVERVIEW Hanwha Renewables, headquartered in Irvine, California, a member of Hanwha Group, a FORTUNE Global 500 firm that is among the eight largest business enterprises in South Korea.
description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Hanwha Renewables, headquartered in Irvine, California, a member of Hanwha Group, a FORTUNE Global 500 firm that is among the eight largest business enterprises in South Korea. Hanwha Renewables designs, builds and manages renewable energy solutions. The company brings a decade of global leadership in renewable energy to North America, combining best-of-world technology, processes, and partnerships to deliver utility-grade energy solutions customized for local energy markets. Hanwha Renewables offers the full spectrum of energy solutions – from power plant development, design, construction, operations, and maintenance. With proven capabilities across the renewable energy value chain, Hanwha Renewables minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Power Marketing Analyst will support the analysis of power market trends, risk assessment, regulatory developments, and other insights that inform the company's power marketing and origination strategy for its solar and energy storage project development portfolio. The role supports the sourcing and execution of offtake opportunities for utility-scale solar, energy storage, and hybrid projects, and helps the Origination & Power Marketing team build strategic partnerships with utilities and other load-serving entities (LSEs) around Power Purchase and Energy Storage Tolling agreements, and alternative revenue structures such as Development Asset Transfers and Build-Transfer Agreements. The ideal candidate brings commercial and regulatory experience in utility-scale solar and energy storage, along with a strong understanding of market dynamics and shifting trends in energy procurement among major offtakers.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Power Marketing and Origination, this role is responsible for data analysis, market research, and coordination with cross-functional teams to help prepare proposals and optimize origination strategies. Over time, the Analyst will develop experience across:

  • The development cycle of new utility-scale solar and energy storage projects
  • New market strategy for greenfield campaigns
  • Future procurement trends of major LSEs, including through Integrated Resource Plans (IRPs)
  • Evolving contracting mechanisms in the solar and storage space
  • Targeted M&A activity

Strong analytical skills, developing market knowledge, and the ability to communicate findings clearly are essential for success in this role. This position is expected to travel up to 10% of the time.

The employee may be required to perform other job-related duties as requested by management. All duties will be assigned in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support execution of client engagement and power marketing strategies across the U.S.
  • Maintain business-tracking systems, including CRM platforms, RFP trackers, and related tools.
  • Prepare or support preparation of presentations for executive and customer briefings.
  • Monitor, track, and summarize load-serving entities' integrated resource and procurement plans.
  • Monitor and help evaluate opportunities across U.S. markets — such as RFPs for potential renewable and energy storage projects — and document and track them for future reference.
  • Coordinate proposal preparation in response to RFPs and bilateral opportunities by identifying, collecting, and organizing required information from subject matter experts across the organization.
  • Monitor public information on executed power purchase, tolling, build-transfer, and related agreements, and document relevant details in shared drive folders and trackers.
  • Monitor RTO and other market working groups for rule changes related to transmission rights, deliverability, and energy markets.
  • Monitor trade associations for relevant regulatory and market developments and share information across the team and organization as appropriate.
  • Assist in modeling and evaluating the impact of market design and topological changes — such as new generation, new storage, and transmission buildouts — on procurement opportunities and future energy prices.
  • Support forecasting of nodal/zonal and OTC energy prices for RTO and bilateral markets across long-term time horizons using fundamental and third-party models and services.
  • Participate as appropriate in standing and ad hoc internal and external meetings.
  • Communicate clearly and succinctly with audiences of different backgrounds during meetings and presentations.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in business, engineering, sustainability, finance, or a related field.
  • Minimum 1–3 years of relevant work experience in the electric utility industry's regulatory or commercial sector.
  • Familiarity with CRM applications and industry platforms such as F1, Procore, LevelTen, Aurora, NPM, or similar tools is a plus.
  • Coursework in at least one of the following areas: power system analysis, power system economics, power system operations and planning, optimization, data analysis, or object-oriented programming. If no relevant coursework, relevant work experience is also considered.
  • Working knowledge of organized and bilateral electricity markets across the U.S.; familiarity with at least one ISO/RTO market is preferred.

COMPENSATION: $90,000 - $105,000 salary
